narration.text: Your document has important things to say. Unfortunately, it is a document. It has no mouth.
Meet Explain-to-Me: a local-first toolkit that turns your words into narrated, captioned explainer videos. Tiny movie studio. Extremely sensible shoes.
Here is the conveyor belt. Start with Markdown, plain text, or a reviewed production manifest.
The toolkit prepares narration, measures the actual speech, then builds the timeline around it. Diagrams, code cards, captions. Everybody arrives together. Nobody gets shoved off the bus.

scenes.title: Give it a desk to dance on

narration.text: For version zero point two, bring a Mac, Node twenty-four or newer, Git, and F F mpeg.

Clone the repository. Install the pinned dependencies. Download the rendering browser once, then run doctor. The README has the exact commands. Doctor checks the tools. It does not check your dance moves.
Make your first video with the bundled manifest and Apple speech. No extra language model required.
Choose a fresh output folder, run the build, and open video dot M P four. Congratulations! Your terminal has entered its film director era.

scenes.title: Give your own ideas a speaking part

narration.text: Next, hand it your own Markdown or text file. Template mode selects source material directly.

Want local model direction and a smoother voice? Install the optional director and Kokoro models, then choose those backends. Setup downloads the tools; inference runs locally. Always review what the model writes.
Your output folder includes the movie, narration audio, captions, manifest, and a report.

Keep the manifest to revise the script. Check the report. Watch and listen before sharing. Automated checks can catch broken timing; they cannot tell whether your explanation is secretly about a potato.

scenes.title: Your agent can hold the clapperboard

lines: Copy the installer prompt from the README

narration.text: Prefer a robot assistant? Copy the quick installer prompt from the README into your coding agent.
It sets up the pinned release, checks prerequisites, and keeps your private stories outside the software checkout. You review the finished movie. The robot gets a tiny imaginary director chair.

scenes.title: Less wall of text. More aha!

narration.text: Version zero point two ships the technical whiteboard style. These cartoons and this music are a custom release showcase.
Grab the code. Explain something useful. Make somebody go, oh, now I get it! Explain-to-Me. Less wall of text. More aha.
